rapport_notes: Handled a direct price objection gracefully and without defensiveness; genuine, funny personal connection ('another Chantel... you see how the universe brings us together').

evidence_quotes.agenda: 'before I hop in too deep did you have any top of mind, concerns or questions that I can answer for you?' — asked immediately, before any logistics questions.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer said 'I'm probably gonna go with a different direction just you were a little bit pricier.' Rep responded with a strong value reframe (all-inclusive pricing) rather than asking a follow-up question to learn more about what she'd been quoted elsewhere.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: 'you are getting two professionally [trained] movers... we don't work with daily contractors' (commit-to-rate) and 'if we... utilize the two and a half to three hours, then that's all you pay for anyway' (beats-it-pay-less).

top_strength: Handled a direct price objection with real poise — instead of getting defensive, reframed the value (all-inclusive pricing, in-house professional movers) and invited the customer to compare quotes transparently, which protects the relationship even though this particular call didn't close.
coaching_note: The price objection was the one and only concern raised on this call — that was the moment to dig deeper ('what specifically felt pricier — the hourly rate or the estimated hours?') instead of moving straight to a value pitch. On-Time Guarantee, Meet Your Mover, and damage coverage were also never mentioned, any of which could have helped justify the price gap.
